atoms.b: All people are ((++different the_same)). In your life, you will have encountered situations where you ((++thought,_felt_or_acted danced,_sounded_or_smelled)) differently from others.
It’s important to remember that just because we think, feel or act a certain way, this ((++might_not_be is_also)) the case for other people.
By considering other people’s feelings, you can build a ((++closer_and_healthier weaker_and_unhappier)) relationship with them.
We can understand people better by paying attention to what they say. These are known as ((++verbal visual)) cues.
We can also notice how people use their bodies to communicate. These are known as ((++physical audio)) cues.

instruction.text: Sort the verbal and physical cues according to whether they show difference or agreement.

atoms.b: What do you think about this other idea?
We can be mindful of what might be happening in the other person’s life that’s influencing how they feel or act. This is called situational ((++awareness blindness)).

instruction.text: Listen and select the facts that might affect the situation.

atoms.a: You are having a conversation with a friend about your holiday abroad. For some reason, she looks sad.
b: She once went to Canada on holiday.

feedback.end: If your friend comes from a family with less money, they might not have the chance to go on holidays. Talking about travel could make them feel left out or upset.

atoms.a: You and a couple of friends are planning a group project. Matthew has been assigned the task of public speaking, but you notice he seems uncomfortable.
b: He left his phone at home.

feedback.end: If Matthew has a fear of speaking to crowds, maybe he could take over some other tasks instead.

atoms.a: You invite your friend to Christmas dinner. He seems uncertain about whether to accept your invitation or not.

hint.text: More than one answer can be correct.

feedback.end: Your friend might feel unsure about joining a Christian celebration because of his beliefs or simply because he’s shy. It’s best to ask him how he feels and what’s on his mind.
